name: v1.5.0
body:
v1.5.0 ships repository-level analysis for supported local invocation paths, including MCP callbacks, tool-list registration, nested tool helpers, and bounded local helper chains. Directory scans enable the repository layer by default; `--no-repository-analysis` provides an explicit opt-out.

This release fixes cache consistency for capabilities and guard suppression, exposes local call-edge and exclusion counts, adds `--include-fixtures`, deduplicates JSON finding output, and reports synthetic recall by hop depth. Resource-boundary detection remains opt-in, with bare-decorator collisions removed.

The release includes public corrections to earlier reachability-rate, recall-bracket, and CVE-attribution claims. Phase 4 labelled-sample brackets and the September corpus snapshot are historical evidence, not a fresh release accuracy estimate.

Limitations remain: guard analysis uses lexical AST structure; general dynamic dispatch and cross-repository reasoning are outside the supported local patterns; LLM output flowing directly to a sink remains NOT COVERED. See the corrected [1.5.0 changelog](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-scan/blob/v1.5.0/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

name: v1.4.0 — Capability model, resource-boundary entry points, test generation
body:
## Capability model

The scanner now records every agent-reachable consequential sink as a Capability, including guarded ones (previously discarded). Four observational states: GUARD_FOUND, REVIEW_REQUIRED, ACCEPTED_DECISION, NOT_ANALYSED. No state asserts safety.

JSON output now includes `capabilities[]`, `capability_count`, `guard_found_count`, `review_required_count` alongside existing `findings[]`. Backward compatible.

## Resource-boundary entry points

FastAPI, Flask, Blueprint, and APIRouter route handlers are now detected as reachable. Control repos: 0 production findings.

## Terminal output

`YOUR AGENT'S BLAST RADIUS` with capability counts shown before finding details.

## Test generation

`fix --with-tests` generates refusal + authorised-execution tests. `--run-tests` executes them (NOT sandboxed).

## Single-source corpus

Version coherence check extracted into testable function. Figure-drift check extended. Corpus figure: 21/22 (95.5%).

## Other

- README rewritten with capability-based output
- 464 tests (was 437)
- Zero runtime dependencies

name: v1.3.1 — fix silent zero-finding PR scans
body:
## Critical fix

The Action's `--changed-only origin/main` mode failed silently on every pull request because `actions/checkout@v4` with default `fetch-depth` does not fetch the base branch. The scan produced 0 findings, no SARIF was uploaded, and no sticky comment was posted — a green check on unscanned code.

**Fix:** the Action now runs `git fetch origin <base_ref> --depth=1` before scanning. The README and `install github` command now document `fetch-depth: 0`.

Found by WO1.11 Phase 6 external verification against a scratch repository consuming `uses: Actenon/actenon-scan@v1`.

### Also includes

- Corpus triage gate fixed to allow recording unfixed false positives (WO1.10)
- verify-claims pyproject-vs-PyPI check corrected (WO1.10-1.11)
- Release gate rewritten to use checkout-at-tag + `uses: ./` (WO1.10)
- Release checklist created (WO1.11)
- v1.3.0 release notes annotated with precision correction (WO1.11)

### Corpus figure

21/22 (95.5%) — 21 true positives, 1 recorded false positive (actions.go:172, tracking issue #81). See [docs/CORPUS_STUDY.md](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-scan/blob/main/docs/CORPUS_STUDY.md).

name: v1.3.0 — TypeScript guard analysis rewritten
body:
> **Correction (2026-07-29):** The corpus precision figure stated in these notes was 22/22 (100%). It has since been corrected to 21/22 (95.5%) after a false positive was reclassified on the merits (the corpus gate was fixed to allow recording unfixed false positives). See [docs/CORPUS_STUDY.md](https://github.com/Actenon/actenon-scan/blob/main/docs/CORPUS_STUDY.md) for the current figure and the full revision history.

---

# v1.3.0 — TypeScript guard analysis rewritten

## Behaviour change

TypeScript guard analysis was unsound before this release. Guard-name substrings appearing in comments, imports, string literals or variable names suppressed findings anywhere below them in the same file, regardless of function boundaries. It has been rewritten with dominance, binding and result-use analysis matching the Python and Go detectors.

TypeScript repositories may report findings that were previously suppressed. Three sink-matching false positives were also fixed (`handler.fetch`, `regex.exec`, arbitrary `.spawn` member calls), which removes findings in the other direction. The net effect per repository is not predictable in advance.

This is a minor version bump, not a patch, because a consumer running `fail-on: high` in CI could go from green to red on an unchanged codebase.

## What changed

- **TypeScript guard analysis rewritten** — 640 lines of new guard analysis code ported from `go.py` and `guards.py`. All five defeated-guard variants (result discarded, guard after sink, dead branch, split branch, try/catch swallow) now flag in TypeScript. Previously all were suppressed by the lexical heuristic.
- **Go assert-style classification fix** — `_is_go_assert_style` used a substring match that misclassified `authorizeBool` (boolean-returning) as assert-style. Fixed with local resolution: the function definition is checked for `panic()` calls.
- **Python try/except dominance fix** — a guard inside a `try` body whose `except` handler catches a broad type with no re-raise no longer dominates the sink.
- **Cross-language parity** — Python, TypeScript, and Go now agree on every defeated-guard variant.
- **`handler.fetch()` false positive fixed** — NET-EGRESS no longer matches `handler.fetch(request)` (MCP handler entry point, not outbound egress). Global `fetch(url)`, `window.fetch(url)`, `globalThis.fetch(url)` still flag.
- **`regex.exec()` false positive fixed** — EXEC-SHELL no longer matches `SAFE.exec(name)` (RegExp.prototype.exec, input validation). `child_process.exec(cmd)` and bare `exec(cmd)` imported from child_process still flag.
- **`pool.spawn()` false positive fixed** — arbitrary `.spawn` member calls no longer flag.
- **Go `PAY-GENERIC-REFUND-GO` and `SECRET-READ-GO` receiver constraints** — no longer match any method named `Refund`/`Charge`/`GetSecretValue` on any receiver.
- **Action `fail-on-unsupported` input** — new input (default `false`) that fails the build when unsupported source files are found.
- **JSON output version field** — JSON output now includes `scanner` and `version` fields.
- **Release gate** — new `release-gate.yml` workflow verifies `uses: Actenon/actenon-scan@<tag>` before v1 advances.

## Corpus precision correction

The corpus precision figure changed from 21/21 (100%) to 21/23 (91%). Two `github-mcp-server` Go findings were triaged for the first time — they were never in the original corpus because the corpus was assembled before Go support shipped. Both are FALSE_POSITIVE: `server.go:286` opens a server-config log file (not model-controlled); `actions.go:172` fetches a GitHub API URL (not directly model-controlled). Counted in the denominator: precision dropped from 100% to 91%. The true-positive count is unchanged at 21.

Full lineage: 63→51→30→28→21→21 (TP unchanged, precision 100%→91%).

## Tests

425 tests passing (was 374 at v1.2.0). 0 self-scan findings.

name: v1.2.0 — Inbound distribution infrastructure
body:
## What's new

### `actenon-scan install github`

New CLI command that generates a safe, non-blocking GitHub Actions workflow:
```bash
uvx actenon-scan install github
```
Supports `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--blocking`, `--baseline`, `--config`. Uses `@v1` stable tag, scoped permissions, no secrets.

### README rewrite

First screen leads with **"What can your AI agent do without permission?"** and three clear routes: run locally, add to GitHub, request a reviewed scan.

### Disclosure & consent infrastructure

- `DISCLOSURE_POLICY.md` — 8-status model, private-first process, publication consent
- `SCAN_ME.md` — maintainer guide for requesting a reviewed scan
- Scan request issue template — structured form with publication preference
- `community-scans/` — directory structure for consented scan reports

### External v1 Action test

New `.github/workflows/external-v1-test.yml` — tests `uses: Actenon/actenon-scan@v1` against a fixture project. Verifies package identity, Go guard recognition, finding count, non-blocking exit. Does NOT use local checkout.

### Fixes

- lychee link check: excluded private actenon-cloud repo (404)
- CORPUS_RESULTS.md: annotated as historical (v0.4.0 era)
- COVERAGE.md TS matrix: corrected (TS has same rule families as Python)

- Corpus claims: 30/30 → 21/21 (matching CORPUS_STUDY.md)

- Clean-venv: install github works, scan works, exit 1 on findings

name: v1.1.4 — Go sink coverage parity (4→9 families) + parity test
body:
## v1.1.4 — Go sink coverage parity (4→9 families) + parity test

Go sink coverage goes from 4 families to 9, matching Python's coverage. Measured recall on the 18-call destructive Go corpus: 9/18 → 16/18 (the remaining 2 are os.Chmod/os.Chown, deliberately not ported).

### New rule families

| Family | Rule ID | Match semantics |
|---|---|---|
| SQL destruction | DATA-DELETE-SQL-GO | Exec/Query on DB receivers; literal DELETE/DROP or non-literal SQL |
| Payments (Stripe) | PAY-STRIPE-REFUND-GO | stripe-go methods (Refund, New, Capture) on receiver names |
| Payments (generic) | PAY-GENERIC-REFUND-GO | Bare method names (Refund, Charge, Transfer) on any receiver |
| Secret read | SECRET-READ-GO | Cloud SDK methods (GetSecretValue, GetParameter). NOT os.Getenv |
| Provider SDK | PROVIDER-SDK-CALL-GO | AWS/GCP/Azure methods (DeleteObject, DeleteBucket) on receiver names |

### Variant misses in existing families

- EXEC-SHELL-GO: + syscall.Exec, syscall.ForkExec
- DATA-DELETE-OS-GO: + os.Truncate, syscall.Unlink, syscall.Rmdir
- os.Chmod/os.Chown: NOT ADDED (proposed as cross-language family, documented)

### Parity test (ITEM 6 — systemic fix)

`tests/test_go_parity.py` — three tests:
- `test_go_recall_corpus`: 18 destructive Go calls, 16/18 expected detected
- `test_sink_family_parity`: fails when a family exists in one language and not another without a registered reason
- `test_go_rule_ids_match_declared_families`: catches rules in code but not in the parity map

This is the systemic fix for the "two code paths diverged" pattern that caused three separate failures in this codebase.

### Re-baselined

| Repo | v1.1.3 | v1.1.4 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic-sdk-go | 6 (6 prod) | 6 (6 prod) | no change |
| go-sdk | 4 (1 prod, 3 ex) | 4 (1 prod, 3 ex) | no change |
| mcp-go | 4 (1 prod, 3 ex) | 4 (1 prod, 3 ex) | no change |
| github-mcp-server | 2 (2 prod) | 2 (2 prod) | no change |

No new findings on any reference repo. Precision on anthropic-sdk-go: still 5/6.

### Verification

- 360 tests passing, 0 self-scan findings
- Clean-venv from wheel: actenon-scan 1.1.4, 6 findings on anthropic-sdk-go, exit 1 by default
- Twine check: PASSED
- Artifacts: `/home/z/my-project/dist/actenon_scan-1.1.4-*`

name: v1.1.3 — ranking prefers model-controlled inputs, Go docs, tier split
body:
## v1.1.3 — ranking + docs fixes

### ITEM 1 (BLOCKER): "Most exposed" now prefers findings with model-controlled inputs

The ranking previously used severity + confidence + destructiveness. A finding with no model-controlled input on the path could be selected as the headline over a finding the model can actually influence.

- `_most_exposed_rank` now includes "has model-controlled inputs" as the FIRST sort criterion (before severity).
- Uses the same call-text parse as the pretty reporter's spotlight — the ranking agrees with what the user sees.
- On anthropic-sdk-go: headline changed from `skills.go:65` (no inputs) to `skills.go:110` (has `dest` as model-controlled input — a sound true positive).
- Regression test: `tests/test_most_exposed_ranking.py` asserts the headline finding has non-empty model-controlled inputs.

### ITEM 2: Constant-path deletes — reported, not suppressed (decision documented)

`os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(e.Workdir, "skills"))` has no model-controlled component on the analysed path. **Decision: REPORT.** The tool cannot verify no other call site reaches the function with model-controlled input. Under-reporting is the worse error. Ranking demotes it below findings with identified inputs. Documented in COVERAGE.md.

### ITEM 3: Go guard vocabulary boundary documented

COVERAGE.md now lists: recognised guard names, method-call form support, `Allow` exclusion (with reasoning), custom guard registration via `--guard`/`guard_patterns` (works for Go exactly as for Python).

### ITEM 4: MCP SDK figures corrected with tier split

| Repo | Production | Example | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| go-sdk | 1 (FP: hardcoded "myserver") | 3 | 4 |
| mcp-go | 1 (borderline: config-controlled) | 3 | 4 |

Both production findings assessed honestly in FINDINGS.md.

### Verification

- 357 tests passing, 0 self-scan findings
- Clean-venv: `actenon-scan 1.1.3`, headline = `skills.go:110` with `Model-controlled inputs: dest`
- Twine check: PASSED

name: v1.1.2 — Go guard recognition, temp-file suppression, explain IR
body:
## v1.1.2 — Go guard recognition, temp-file suppression, explain IR

Three correctness fixes for Go support, verified against anthropic-sdk-go, modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk, mark3labs/mcp-go, and github-mcp-server.

### ITEM 1 (BLOCKER): Go detector now recognises guards

The Go detector previously had zero guard analysis — every Go finding printed "Guard evidence: none found on the analysed path" without any search being performed. This was false for every Go finding the tool had ever emitted.

- Reuses the guard vocabulary from `guards.py` (no parallel Go list). Handles Go's camelCase convention: `checkPermission` matches `check_permission`.
- Dominance, binding, result-use, defeated-guard handling. Assert-style guards don't require binding.
- False negatives are worse than false positives: if unsure, does NOT suppress.
- 8 soundness tests in `tests/test_go_guard_soundness.py`.

### ITEM 2: Temp-file false positives suppressed

3 of 8 findings on anthropic-sdk-go were false positives from deferred cleanup of self-created temp files. Now suppressed when the argument is assigned from `os.CreateTemp`/`os.MkdirTemp`/`.Name()` within the same function. Anchored to assignment source, not to defer or "tmp".

### ITEM 3: explain IR works for Go

`explain` previously showed `<module-level>` (Python terminology) and `(none identified)` for model-controlled inputs. Now uses tree-sitter to extract the real function name, parameters, and guard evidence.

### ITEM 4: Re-baselined numbers

| Repo | Before (v1.1.1) | After (v1.1.2) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| anthropic-sdk-go | 8 | 6 | -2 (temp-file FPs) |
| go-sdk | 4 | 4 | no change |
| mcp-go | 4 | 4 | no change |
| github-mcp-server | 2 | 2 | no change |

No repo had a count increase from guard recognition.

### Clean-venv verification

```
$ pip install actenon-scan[go]==1.1.2
$ actenon-scan --version
actenon-scan 1.1.2
$ actenon-scan scan anthropic-sdk-go ; echo $?
```

name: v1.1.1 — regression fix release
body:
## v1.1.1 — regression fix release

v1.1.0 shipped with a P0 regression: the CLI `--fail-on` default was changed from `medium` to `none`, which meant a scan that found 8 unguarded consequential actions exited 0 — passing CI silently. v1.1.1 reverts the default and fixes two additional items.

### ITEM 1 (P0 REGRESSION): CLI `--fail-on` default reverted to `medium`

**What broke:** `actenon-scan scan .` on a repo with 8 high-severity findings exited 0. v1.0.0 exited 1 on the same tree.

**Root cause:** v1.1.0 changed the CLI default to `none` to match `action.yml`. The inconsistency was real, but resolved in the wrong direction — the CLI has no other machine-readable signal, so its exit code IS the status.

**Fix:**
- `cli.py`: default is now `medium` (matching v1.0.0 + semgrep/bandit/eslint/shellcheck convention). Comment explains why the CLI and action.yml intentionally differ.
- `action.yml`: stays at `none` (has sticky PR comment + SARIF upload). Comment added.
- README: documents the full exit code contract including the deliberate CLI/Action difference.
- 3 new tests pin the default.

### ITEM 2: docs/COVERAGE.md stale Go claims fixed

Every scan prints "See docs/COVERAGE.md for supported architectures and analysis limits." v1.1.0 added Go support, but COVERAGE.md still said "The scanner supports Python and TypeScript but not Go." A successful Go scan directed the user to a document telling them Go was unsupported.

**Fixed:**
- Line 270: language support updated to include Go.
- Line 546: benchmark table `github-mcp-server | 0 (Go unsupported)` → `2 (Go)`. Re-scanned the pinned SHA (eb088dfe) with 1.1.0: 2 findings across 131 Go files.
- Lines 565-570: "Limitation: Go-based MCP servers" → "Go-based MCP servers (now supported)" with actual findings listed.
- Line 589: coverage verdicts "NOT SUPPORTED" → "COVERED".
- docs/CORPUS_RESULTS.md: two-language claims updated.

### ITEM 3: Go findings no longer show Python decorator syntax

`pretty.py` `_decorator_or_function` guessed `@mcp.tool() or @tool` based on the file path — with no language check. A Go finding rendered with Python decorator syntax.

**Fix:**
- `GoFinding` + `Finding` dataclasses now carry `reachability_reason`.
- Go detector populates it (`agent_framework_import`, `tool_registration`, or both).
- `_decorator_or_function` renders the real reason for Go; path-guess now ONLY applies to `.py` files.

**Verified on github-mcp-server:** `Reachable by: agent framework import` (was `@mcp.tool() or @tool`).

### ITEM 4: Exit code contract documented

README now has a "CLI vs Action" table explaining why the defaults intentionally differ, with a "Do not fix them back into alignment" note.

### Verification

- `pytest tests/` → 348 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
- Self-scan: 0 findings on own repo (39 files)
- Clean-venv install from PyPI: `actenon-scan 1.1.1`, 2 findings on github-mcp-server, exit 1 by default, `Reachable by: agent framework import`
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/actenon-scan/1.1.1/

### Migration notes

If you relied on v1.1.0's `none` default (findings not failing the build), pass `--fail-on none` explicitly. This is the correct behavior for triaged repos with baselines, but should not be the default — a scanner that finds findings and exits 0 passes CI silently.

name: v1.1.0 — first-touch readiness
body:
## Release: v1.1.0 — first-touch readiness

Bumps version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0. This release captures **three rounds of audit fixes** that close the gap between "works on the happy path" and "works flawlessly end-to-end when external users try it."

### What's in this release

**44 fixes total, 61 new regression tests, 347 tests passing** (was 286 before any audit).

| Round | PR | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| 1: Code-level audit | #57 | 7 P0s + 9 P1s (action.yml SARIF, suppression path, BOM, parallel cache, Windows paths, README consistency, classifier, perf-fixture, CONTRIBUTING, fix.py imports, explain.py docs refs) |
| 2: User-story audit | #57 | 11 P0s + 4 M items (fix.py real API, fix.py calls not TODOs, action.yml FINDINGS_COUNT, action.yml PR_NUMBER, --changed-only covers .ts/.go, suppress.py both syntaxes, pyproject.toml [project.urls], __init__.py reads pyproject.toml, sarif.py helpUri+tags+CWE/OWASP, pre-commit additional_dependencies, _parse_location rejects negative lines, fix.py refuses non-Python files, baseline subcommand, --all flag, config-based custom sinks/reachability docs) |
| 3: Three-persona first-touch audit | #58 | 7 P0s + 3 cross-persona (cache bypasses baseline, init overwrites config, fix nested-block indent, --fail-on default none, --changed-only empty diff, public Python API, cache relocation, community files, CHANGELOG deprecation policy) |
| Cloudflare fix | #64 | Minimal Worker so the Workers Builds check passes |

### Highlights

- **Public Python API**: `from actenon_scan import scan_path` now works. New `actenon_scan.api` module with `__all__` and stability docstring. `py.typed` marker for PEP 561.
- **Cache no longer pollutes workspace**: defaults to XDG cache home instead of `.actenon-scan-cache/` in the scanned dir. `ACTENON_SCAN_CACHE_DIR` env var + `--cache-dir` flag.
- **Cache no longer bypasses baseline**: the cache-hit path now re-applies baseline + suppression from the current sets on every hit.
- **`--fail-on` default is `none`**: matches action.yml. New users no longer see exit 1 on their first scan.
- **`init` merges instead of overwrites**: preserves `exclude`/`sinks`/`reachability` keys. `--force` restores overwrite.
- **`fix` uses the real actenon-kernel API**: `from actenon_kernel import verify_pccb` (was the non-existent `from actenon import verify_proof`).
- **`fix` nested-block indentation**: guard inserted at sink's own indent when inside with/for/if.
- **`--all` flag on explain/brief**: 50 findings no longer = 50 commands.
- **`baseline` subcommand**: generates baselines (was referenced by `adopt` but didn't exist).
- **SARIF rule metadata**: `helpUri`, `properties.tags` (security/ai-agent/cwe-*/owasp-*), `properties.cwe`, `properties.owasp`.
- **Pre-commit TS/Go hooks**: `additional_dependencies` so they actually install tree-sitter.
- **Community files**: ISSUE_TEMPLATE, PR_TEMPLATE, CODEOWNERS, dependabot, FUNDING.
- **CHANGELOG deprecation policy**: public API = `actenon_scan.api`; breaking changes require major bump + 2-release deprecation cycle.

### Three-persona readiness

| Persona | Before audits | After v1.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Individual developer | ~70% | **~95%** |
| Company engineering team | ~40% | ~55% |
| Agent integrations | ~20% | ~50% |

### Verification

- `pytest tests/` -> 347 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
- `actenon-scan scan .` -> 0 findings on own repo (39 files)
- All 7 claim scripts green
- CI: 15/15 green on main (including Cloudflare Workers build)

### Migration notes

- **`--fail-on` default changed**: if you relied on the CLI defaulting to `medium`, pass `--fail-on medium` explicitly.
- **Cache location changed**: old `.actenon-scan-cache/` dirs in your repos can be deleted; the cache now lives under `~/.cache/actenon-scan/`. Set `ACTENON_SCAN_CACHE_DIR` for CI persistence.
- **`init` no longer overwrites**: existing `.actenon-scan.json` is preserved. Use `--force` for the old behavior.

### What's next (v1.2.0 — enterprise readiness)

The round-3 audit identified these remaining items for a follow-up PR:
- SBOM + SLSA provenance in `publish.yml`
- `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` + `docs/API_REFERENCE.md` + `docs/UPGRADE.md` + `docs/INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md`
- `--sarif-output` flag (eliminate double scan in action.yml)
- `categories` + `brand` kwargs on `scan_path`
- `load_rules_from_dict` + `register_reachability_signal` API
